definitions.explanation: A ball-shaped Japanese snack made from a wheat flour batter filled with diced octopus, cooked in a specially molded pan. Typically topped with sauce, mayonnaise, dried bonito flakes, and dried seaweed powder.

examples.japanese: たこ{焼|や}き⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{食|た}べよう→食べる：00396_taberu⟧。

⟦{屋台|やたい}→屋台：10549_yatai⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{焼|や}きたて→焼きたて：16735_yakitate⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧たこ{焼|や}き⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{買|か}って→買う：00489_kau⟧、⟦ソース→ソース：17673_soosu⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦マヨネーズ→マヨネーズ：11129_mayoneezu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦かけて→かける：00854_kakeru⟧⟦{食|た}べた→食べる：00396_taberu⟧。
examples.english: I bought freshly cooked takoyaki from a street stall and ate it with sauce and mayonnaise.

notes:
Composed of たこ (octopus) + ⟦{焼|や}き→焼く：01123_yaku⟧ (grilled/cooked). A ball-shaped snack made from wheat flour batter with diced octopus inside, cooked in a specially molded pan.

CULTURAL NOTE:
Originating from ⟦{大阪|おおさか}→大阪：09779_oosaka⟧, takoyaki is one of Japan's most iconic street foods. Osaka residents take great pride in their takoyaki, and many ⟦{大阪|おおさか}→大阪：09779_oosaka⟧ households own a たこ{焼|や}き{器|き} (takoyaki maker).
